en: Then, on the final day, the sacrifice to Caṇḍeśvara must be performed;
at its beginning, a mandala is prescribed, which is called the "half-moon. || 1 ||
Having abandoned the fifth part of the measured circumference,
one should rotate the remaining thread, equal to the measure, like a half-moon.
In its center, one should draw an eight-petalled lotus with a pericarp,
measuring twelve finger-breadths or else the span of a hand.
Having placed the seat upon that yoga-pedestal,
the Guru should then install the deity Caṇḍeśvara, who stands upon the Śarva-Śarva square.
Then, having again duly assigned the limbs of the Vidyā to him, he should further assign the Weapon-mantra to the quarters beginning with the southeast (āgneya). || 5 ||
Having worshipped them with perfumes, flowers, and the like, as well as various kinds of food and ornaments,
one should satisfy them with the remnants of the sacrifice by offering one hundred and eight portions.
Afterwards, having gratified the heart and all the other [limbs] one by one in sequence with twenty oblations of clarified butter, he should ask for forgiveness.
One should prepare only such things as are suitable for Caṇḍeśvara for the purpose of worship;
however, one who desires to follow the prescribed rule must not consume anything situated within a line of red powder.
Therefore, any other substance offered to the deity should also be cast into the fathomless water specifically for Caṇḍeśa.
Therefore, for those who act otherwise and violate the command of Śiva, Caṇḍeśvara is the punisher; he is the lord even over those who have been initiated.
For those who have taken refuge in Caṇḍeśvara, there is no cause for fear;
therefore, those whose devotion is undiminished have resorted to the path of Śiva.
Then, at the conclusion of the watch of the night, on a ground marked with svastikas,
he should perform the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha-snāna) for himself and for the initiated disciple.
Having bathed with the jar presided over by Śiva, which removes all evil deeds, the wise one should thereafter worship the Guru along with his attendants.
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, the Caṇḍayāga-paṭala, in the Svāyambhuva-sūtra-saṅgraha.
